_wording_note: Conclusions were written at run time. The paper (v1.0) uses calibrated wording: the collapse is consistent with error magnitude alone; the ~0.44 floor applies to elementwise ternary rounding of Gaussian weights; calibration-based PTQ was not tested; the gap is not concentrated in the coarsest code (later levels not localized further).
_source: standalone Colab cell after section 12 (procedure in paper Section 6), Colab A100; values copied from the cell output
description: Per-puzzle generation on the full 2000-puzzle test set; true coarsest code = tokenizer encode of the test solution (S-FLM valid split, prefix match 100%).
counterfactual: Ternary with FP's coarse-code accuracy: 0.855*74.58 + 0.145*61.80 = 72.7% (+1.1 pt). The coarse code explains ~1 of the 14.5 pt gap.
conclusion: Hypothesis that the gap comes from the single coarsest decision is refuted. A wrong coarsest code still often yields the correct board (75% FP, 62% ternary): coarse codes are not uniquely decisive. The gap is spread over later levels. Also: the earlier 'FP 95.5% coarse TF accuracy' was measured on holdout_seqs, which are part of the official FP model's training data (biased); on test FP gets 85.5%.
